clue.text: This should be reduced in development, but in practice often isn't!

definitions.text: This should be reduced in development, but in practice often isn't!

parts.words: This should be reduced in development, but in practice often isn't
parts.note: a tiny photographic image is meant to be shrunk when the film is processed, yet the long word naming it is anything but reduced

explanation.surface: A grumble about some plan or budget that ought to shrink as a project develops but rarely does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' is the photographic sense: processing film. The joke is that the image is minute while its fifteen-letter name is not cut down at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph reduced to microscopic size, as on microfilm, is by design shrunk during processing.

clue.text: Seriously deft or adaptive? We are

definitions.text: Seriously deft or adaptive? We are

indicators.note: adaptive suggests adjusting or reshaping, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Home-improvement enthusiasts boast of being both skilful and adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SERIOUSLY DEFT OR are rearranged, signalled by 'adaptive', and the whole clue doubles as the boast of home handymen.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur home-improvers who fix things themselves would claim to be deft and adaptable.

clue.text: Innovative clue: "Lot in coven?"

indicators.note: innovative means made new or changed, so the letters of the following words are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: A setter praises a clever clue that asks what you call a lot of witches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innovative' rearranges CLUE plus LOT IN COVEN; and 'coven' is itself the term for a gathering of witches, which is what the clue's question illustrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Coven is a word for a group of witches, the kind of grammatical term naming a lot of creatures.

clue.text: What orientates unorthodox conditional changes may be viewed here

definitions.text: conditional changes may be viewed here

indicators.note: unorthodox means unconventional or out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what gives direction to strange shifts in circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conditional changes' is not about grammar: it means changes in the conditions outside, which instruments at such a site record.
explanation.definitionFit: A site with instruments recording atmospheric conditions lets changes in them be observed.

clue.text: An anemometer? I'll be blown

definitions.meaning: an anemometer is a device measuring breeze speed, so a gauge of moving air
a flute or trumpet is played by blowing, a musical device sounded by breath

explanation.surface: A gadget for measuring gusts, followed by a startled exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll be blown' looks like an exclamation of surprise, but it is the voice of a trumpet or clarinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a gauge of breezes and a musical device sounded by breath fit the phrase.

clue.text: Publications abroad for sister to get undercover investigators southwards

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for
a nun is a religious sister
CIA men are American intelligence agents working undercover
taken as written
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Foreign announcements telling a nun to bring in some secret agents heading south.
explanation.definitionFit: Proclamations issued in Spanish-speaking countries, especially by rebels, are public pronouncements made abroad.

clue.text: Work ethic following a payment matey's pocketed (thus?)

indicators.note: pocketed means held inside, so the friendly word is put around the other pieces

parts.note: matey means friendly, as does pally

indicators.note: following places the reworked letters after the payment

parts.note: taken as written
rent is a regular payment for housing

indicators.note: work as a verb means to shape or knead, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diligent attitude after some payment is pocketed by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work ethic' reads as one phrase, but 'Work' is a verb turning ETHIC into HETIC. The definition is the bracketed '(thus?)': a word set aside in brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: The bracketed thus shows a word inserted as an aside, which is how something said in brackets appears.

clue.text: Essentially brief's doing what bra does for occupant of cell

indicators.note: doing here means performing the job of enclosing and supporting, so the core letters go around the chest
essentially means at its core, so the word that follows loses its outer letters

parts.note: a bra is worn to support the bosom

explanation.surface: Some underwear sentence about briefs behaving like a bra, for a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief's' suggests underwear, which the bra image reinforces; 'cell' is biological, not a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny particle making proteins lives inside a biological cell, so it occupies one.

clue.text: Raid on antagonist

indicators.note: antagonist suggests opposing and disrupting, so the letters before it are shaken up

explanation.surface: An attack mounted against an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: RAID ON rearranged gives the answer, and the whole clue describes what it is: an incursion against a foe.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion is a hostile advance into enemy territory, a raid on an opponent.

clue.text: On the other hand — one's left restricts right, which is cruel

indicators.note: restricts means confines, so the qualifying word closes round the letter for right

parts.note: but means on the other hand
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A contrast is drawn: someone's left hand confines the right one, which is cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and cruel are synonyms, describing harsh, pitiless behaviour.

clue.text: Fast food preserver contracts nasty disease

indicators.note: contracts here means takes in, so the canner holds the disease letters

parts.note: a tinner is someone who tins food, preserving it
VD is the abbreviation for venereal disease

explanation.surface: Someone preserving food catches an unpleasant illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like catching a disease, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready meal heated and eaten in front of the set is quick convenience food.

clue.text: Capable of doing no more?

definitions.meaning: being equal to a task, as in 'not fit for the job'
as a limit, meaning not exceeding, as in 'seats at most ten'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both equal to a task and as a maximum of, two familiar senses.

clue.text: Retail IOU, b-li-v-!

parts.note: read believe for credit and then drop every e, and you get the gapped spelling printed in the clue

explanation.surface: A shop's voucher, written in a strange gapped spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Believe is CREDIT; the dashes show it with no E's, so CREDIT NOT E.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip a shop gives for returned goods is a promise of value, effectively an IOU.

clue.text: See 5
Respectively, what may be opencast and ignoring consequences

parts.note: something that may be open is a door
something that may be cast is a die, as in the die is cast

explanation.surface: Mining talk about strip pits and reckless decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Respectively' tells you to split opencast into open and cast and find a word for each.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate do-everything attitude disregards risk, so recklessly ignoring outcomes.

clue.text: Bottom magnitude blocked the court (Law and History)!

indicators.note: blocked means stopped up, so the size word plugs the middle of the bottom word

parts.note: ass is a slang word for the buttocks
size means magnitude

explanation.surface: Something enormous blocked a court, labelled as law and history.
explanation.walkthrough: (Law and History) are dictionary labels: the ASSIZES were former periodic county courts in England and Wales, abolished in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical English criminal courts held periodically in each county were known by this name.

clue.text: See 4
"O", might it be, "My darling …" to begin with?

definitions.meaning: O is the symbol of nil in tennis, so its letter is zero score
an amorous note might open with a tender greeting

explanation.surface: A romantic note opens with a sigh and an endearment.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis, written O, so O is a letter of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: O is the letter for nil score, and a romantic note opens with an endearment.

clue.text: Chief generator at the house

parts.note: a mother generates offspring, and ma is mother
in means at home

explanation.surface: A power source for a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generator' suggests electrics, but it is MA, a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal and chief share the sense of most important.

clue.text: One's out to take catch, meaning the rest of the team's standing back

parts.note: drift means general meaning, as in 'catch my drift'

indicators.note: standing back means set in reverse, so the number word is read backwards

parts.note: a cricket team is eleven; the rest after one is out is ten

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: one batter dismissed by a catch while the others hang back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's out' sounds like cricket, but it describes a fishing net put out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing net left out in the sea to drift is set to take a catch of fish.

clue.text: See 3
Time many do for reform

indicators.note: for reform means to be reshaped, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of people do time behind bars to reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week is a span of time.

clue.text: Witty reference to office accident? Point taken

indicators.note: taken means removed, so the abbreviation's letters come out

parts.note: a paper cut is a typical office injury

explanation.surface: A clever remark about an office mishap; the point is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point taken' reads as agreement, but it removes P and T from PAPERCUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An insightful, pithy remark or comment is a witty observation.

clue.text: Have aspirations, presumably to avoid these!

definitions.text: Have aspirations, presumably to avoid these!

parts.note: to own is to have
goals are aims or aspirations

explanation.surface: Ambitious people want to steer clear of self-defeating errors.
explanation.walkthrough: A football team aspires to score, so presumably not into its own net.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls put into one's own net in football are what a team aiming to score would avoid.
